solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sunlamp deployed around a lounger

indicators.note: to deploy is to spread out and arrange troops, so the letters are set out in a new order
going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sunbed lamp is angled over someone stretched out on a lounger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounger' looks like garden furniture, but it is a person. PAULSMAN (Paul's man) is an old word for an idler who hung about the aisles of St Paul's Cathedral in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Paul's man was a loafer of old London who spent idle hours in the cathedral's middle aisle, an idler.

clue.text: Agreement reportedly ready to go

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the words are spoken

blocks.note: bags packed means ready to leave

explanation.surface: Someone says a deal is all set to proceed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready to go' sounds like a description of the agreement, but it is the sound-alike: someone with bags packed is ready to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal treaty or deal between parties, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Like some mites damaged acorn and dahlia

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Garden pests have chewed through an acorn and a dahlia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like mites ruining plants, which disguises that the two plant names are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Mites belong to the arachnid class with spiders, so they can be described as spiderlike, arachnoidal.

clue.text: Fixing waterworks complaints our working record initially is competent

indicators.note: something working is in operation and moving about, so its letters are rearranged
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a log is a written record
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A plumber claims a good track record in sorting out complaints about the water system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waterworks' is British slang for the urinary system, so this is medicine, not plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Urology is the medical speciality treating disorders of the urinary tract, jokingly called the waterworks.

clue.text: What might be left on a cross steer?

definitions.text: What might be left on a cross steer?

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
a zo (also dzo) is a Himalayan cross between a yak and a cow

explanation.surface: A cowboy wonders what might be left hanging on an angry bullock.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a lasso may be left on a steer, and a crossbred steer is a zo. 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazo is a variant spelling of lasso, the rope noose thrown to catch cattle.

clue.text: School admitted trouble in the playground?

blocks.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
took in, admitted, as a school takes pupils

explanation.surface: A school owns up to bad behaviour at break time.
explanation.walkthrough: The playground and the question mark hint that the word is slang, the kind of informal talk heard among children.
explanation.definitionFit: Schtook is British slang for being in difficulty or in a mess, a colloquial word for trouble.

clue.text: French settler living a simple life, missing the centre of Paris

indicators.note: what is missing has gone, so a letter is taken away
the centre is the middle, so just the middle letter is wanted

blocks.note: Arcadia is the idealised land of simple rustic living
the middle letter of the five-letter city

explanation.surface: A French colonist enjoys rural simplicity far from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The French setting makes Paris look like part of the picture; it is only there to supply its middle letter for removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acadians were the colonists of Acadia, the old French colony in what is now eastern Canada.

clue.text: Trouble on second stage of HS2 project

indicators.note: the second stage is the second step along, so the second character is chosen

blocks.note: the second character of the rail project's name
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Problems hit the second phase of the HS2 rail scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: HS2 is a controversial British high-speed rail line built in phases. 'On' places the trouble after the letter, as in an across clue the second piece follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail can mean to move or jut out boldly, close to the verb sense of project, to stand forward.

clue.text: What has vehicle going around following street round area?

definitions.text: What has vehicle going around following street round area?

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another
turning around faces the other way, so the letters run backwards
what follows comes after, so one piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
A is the abbreviation for area
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A riddle: what device has a car going around, tracking streets across a district?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: a satnav guides a vehicle around, following streets about an area.
explanation.definitionFit: A satnav is a satellite navigation unit that directs drivers street by street through a district.

clue.text: Odd MAGA thinking shows this more than once

definitions.text: thinking shows this more than once

indicators.note: something odd is strange or out of the usual, so the letters are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: the American political slogan, taken as letters

explanation.surface: A dig at strange political reasoning that keeps repeating itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the sound, not the politics: the word 'thinking' contains the nasal 'ng' sound twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Agma is the phoneticians' name for the velar nasal 'ng' sound, heard twice in the clue's word thinking.

clue.text: Aromatic liquid left in potato peel losing water

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it, so part of a word is dropped

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
aloo is the Indian word for potato, familiar from curry menus
taken as written
pee is informal for urine, water in the medical sense

explanation.surface: A fragrant fluid is found in potato skins that have been dried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potato peel' reads as one thing but splits into two pieces, and 'water' is the slang sense of urine, taken out of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Linalool is a fragrant alcohol found in lavender and coriander oils, used in perfumes.

clue.text: Chief area introducing worthless food crop

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring something inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: arch means chief, as in archenemy
A is the abbreviation for area
raca is a biblical term of contempt meaning worthless

explanation.surface: The main growing region brings in a crop that earns nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: RACA comes from the Sermon on the Mount, where calling someone 'raca' (empty, worthless) is condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: The arracacha is an Andean plant grown for its starchy edible root, like a parsnip.

clue.text: Opera mate grasps story regularly, but not too much

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold tight, so a pair of pieces holds another between them
at regular intervals, so every other letter is picked

blocks.note: Manon is an opera by Massenet
the second and fourth letters
oppo is British slang for a friend or colleague

explanation.surface: A friend at the opera follows the plot now and then, but without overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opera mate' together does the grasping, so the selected letters sit between the two names. 'But' looks like a link word, yet it is part of the definition, matching 'ma'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ma non troppo is the Italian musical direction meaning but not excessively, as in allegro ma non troppo.

clue.text: Local hack staff who will trade in coal

blocks.note: hoast is a Scots and Northern dialect word for a cough, a hack
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A regional journalist hires workers to deal in coal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist, but it is a cough, and 'Local' flags the dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoastmen were members of the Newcastle guild that controlled shipping and selling of coal on the Tyne.

clue.text: Fool cutting most of the cotton for export

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within another
most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the three-letter word without its last letter
a clot is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot trims down most of the cotton bound for overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like trimming fabric, but it means inserting: the fool cuts into the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: T-cloth was a plain cotton fabric stamped with a T, made in Britain for the Indian and Chinese trade.

clue.text: Idiot to judge spiritual knowledge

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
a nana is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Calling someone an idiot for judging the mystic's wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' attaches the idiot after the judge's letter; 'judge' looks like a verb but is the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Jnana is the Hindu term for knowledge gained through meditation and insight, the path of wisdom.

clue.text: Perhaps still radioactive, covered in polonium

indicators.note: something covered in a coat is wrapped by it, so one piece is inside another

blocks.note: Po is the chemical symbol for polonium
hot is slang for radioactive

explanation.surface: Something coated in polonium may well still be giving off radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like the adverb 'yet'; it is the noun, a single frame from a film, with 'Perhaps' flagging an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, often a frame from a film, so a photo is one example.

clue.text: Canada’s wrong in present conveyance of the law

indicators.note: something wrong is not as it should be, so the letters are out of order
being in something means being enclosed by it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
pr is a dictionary abbreviation for present

explanation.surface: Canada is said to be mistaken about how its present law is conveyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveyance' looks like a legal transfer of property; it is a vehicle, and 'the law' is the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A panda car is a British police patrol car, named for its old two-tone paintwork, transport for officers.

clue.text: Daughter concealing a very good opal

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: a daughter is a girl
taken as written
so means very, as in so kind

explanation.surface: A daughter hides a fine opal from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' reads as one phrase, but 'very' belongs to the wordplay and 'good' to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A girasol is a fire opal, prized for the play of light within it, a valued gemstone.

clue.text: Took steps endlessly about air flight safety item

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off
about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: strode means walked with long steps
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aviation safety device involves walking round in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' looks like air travel; it is a flight of stairs, which 'Took steps' also hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair rod holds the carpet in place at the back of each step so nobody trips on the staircase.

clue.text: Tumour again formed around edges of omentum

indicators.note: something formed has been shaped anew, so the letters take a new arrangement
the edges are the outermost parts, so only the first and last letters count
around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A growth has come back near the omentum, the abdominal fatty membrane.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'formed' look like the tumour growing, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An angioma is a benign growth made of blood or lymph vessels, a kind of tumour.

clue.text: Religious convert once more round Scots isle

indicators.note: to go round something is to enclose it

blocks.note: mo is an archaic form of more, flagged by 'once'
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: A convert goes back around a Scottish island again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once more' looks like 'again'; here 'once' means formerly, so it is the old word for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Marranos were Spanish and Portuguese Jews forced to convert to Christianity in the late Middle Ages.

clue.text: Can material be in second language

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
is is a form of the verb be
kit is equipment, the materials for a job

explanation.surface: A question about whether some fabric could serve as a second tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second language' reads as one phrase but splits: 'second' is the short moment and 'language' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Miskito is the tongue of the Miskito people of the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua and Honduras.

clue.text: Easily overlooked one share supported by current MP

blocks.note: shr is an abbreviation for share
I is the symbol for electric current
taken as written

explanation.surface: A backbencher is easy to ignore despite owning a stake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts the share on top of what follows. 'One' looks like the numeral but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp is slang for a tiny person, someone small enough to be missed in a crowd.

clue.text: Cuckoo mother answering in a lively manner

blocks.note: the ani is a black tropical American bird of the cuckoo family
ma is informal for mother
answering to means responding to

explanation.surface: A crazy mother replies with plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like 'mad', an anagram signal, but here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Animato is the Italian musical direction telling players to perform with animation and spirit.

clue.text: What was plucked orchid unfortunately died

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events goes awry, so the letters go astray

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A picked orchid has sadly withered away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucked' looks like picked flowers; it is the plucking of strings. 'Was' points to an old instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A dichord was an ancient two-stringed instrument whose strings were sounded by plucking.

clue.text: Technique mostly holds right sound of bagpipes

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the last letter is lost
to hold is to keep within, so one piece is put inside

blocks.note: skill is technique or expertise
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Piping technique largely depends on getting the sound right.
explanation.walkthrough: The bagpipe surface makes 'right sound' look like a phrase; 'right' is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirl is the shrill wailing noise produced by a set of Highland pipes.

clue.text: Deck party held by Australian navy

indicators.note: something held is gripped all round, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for Australian
a do is a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A celebration on a ship's deck is hosted by the Australian navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a ship's floor, which the navy surface encourages; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to decorate it, as in deck the halls, which is what adorning means.

clue.text: South African men accepting positive work

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: ou is South African slang for a man, plural ous
P is the abbreviation for positive

explanation.surface: Men in South Africa agree to take on a constructive job.
explanation.walkthrough: OU is Afrikaans-derived slang for a bloke, common in South African English.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a creative piece, especially a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: Yogurt-like cheese of small Greek island

blocks.note: skyr is a thick Icelandic cultured dairy product
o' is a shortened form of of
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A dairy product comes from a little Aegean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Greek cheese like feta, but the cheese is Icelandic.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyros is an island in the Aegean Sea, the largest of the Sporades group.

clue.text: Take in short American story

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it
short means cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for take, from the Latin recipe on prescriptions
Yank is slang for an American

explanation.surface: Believe a brief tale from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like 'believe' or 'deceive'; 'Take' is the prescription letter and 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long rambling tale, often embroidered, told for entertainment.

clue.text: Northern cormorant missing last sea reef

indicators.note: without the final part, so the ending letter is lost

blocks.note: scart is a Scots and Northern English word for a cormorant

explanation.surface: A northern seabird is gone from its last rocky outcrop in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern' flags a dialect word for the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a rocky outcrop or cliff; in northern usage also a rocky ledge in the sea.

clue.text: Bread eaten by high Inca chiefs

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece is enclosed
someone high is intoxicated and muddled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
pita is a flat bread

explanation.surface: Flatbread is eaten by the lofty leaders of the Inca empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Inca chiefs' looks like the definition; 'high' is the anagram signal, 'Inca' the letters, and only 'chiefs' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitani is the Italian plural of capitano, a captain or head man, so leaders.

clue.text: Male potoo ran around bird’s-nest?

indicators.note: moving around means getting turned about, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A male potoo, a tropical nightbird, runs around its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird surface makes 'bird's-nest' look literal; the question mark signals it is a plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotropa is the genus of yellow bird's-nest, a pale flowering plant without chlorophyll.

clue.text: File on the Royal Mile is coming between king and prince

indicators.note: to come between two things is to sit inside their pair

blocks.note: R is for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
P is the abbreviation for prince

explanation.surface: A procession on Edinburgh's Royal Mile passes between a king and a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Mile is Edinburgh's main old-town street, flagging a Scots word. 'File' looks like a line of people; it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Risp is a Scots word for a rasp, a coarse metal-working tool, used in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Dog runs by where one sees lizards around noon

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped by another
by means beside, so the pieces are set next to each other

blocks.note: Komodo is the Indonesian island home of the Komodo dragon
N is the abbreviation for noon
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dog dashes past a spot where lizards bask at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like the dog's action, but it is a single letter placed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The komondor is a large Hungarian sheepdog breed with a distinctive corded white coat.
